title: The Missing Layer
says: A busy board for the browser. Every knob is something this tab can already do.
what: The site holds no application and no data. It gives a grammar, and each browser that opens it is one live state. This file is the whole board: the one script on the site is a generator that reads it and turns the shapes it knows into running code.
rule: The board is one screen: no scroll, no navigation. The page the loaded JSONs make may scroll. On load only the title and one line are visible. No text is ever run as code; the page asks the browser to refuse it. Only shapes the generator knows become code.

doors.cover: The page opens on a title and one line. The word explore in the line leads to /explore. The board is built behind it. Touch the title to go in, or call board.enter().
doors.knobs: Touch a store, touch a verb, type into Name and Value, touch Do. Undo takes back the last thing done.
doors.shape: Type or paste JSON into Shape and touch Generate. A shape is one of: a run {"store", "verb", "Name", "Value"}; bare steps {"steps": [...]}; a list of shapes; or a whole contract like this file, which rebuilds the board.
doors.round trip: Everything that runs is listed under Ran as the shape it was, with the code it stood for. Touch a line to put it back in Shape, or touch Hand back for all of it in order, then Generate.
doors.floppy: Save downloads what the board is and holds as plain JSON; Load takes the files back and rebuilds it. The same through Shape: {"keep": true} writes the floppies into Shape, {"keep": {"size": 4000}} makes each at most that many bytes, and Generate takes them back, in any order. A floppy holds records: the board, each store, each thing held. It never holds code; the generator rebuilds from the records. From a script: board.serialize(size) and board.deserialize(floppies). By address: /serialize downloads the floppies; /deserialize asks whether to download a copy first, then takes the files. Rebuilding wipes everything first: the site goes back to the board it shipped with, every kept store empty, and is then rebuilt from the floppies.
doors.matrix: The site ships sheets beside the board; "ships" names them. A sheet is a JSON that says what exists and what moves, and names no device; "sheet" is everything one can say. Through Shape: {"load": "email.wire"} loads one from the site, a sheet pasted whole loads itself, {"unload": "email.wire"} takes one out. Nothing happens because a sheet was loaded: each time the loaded set changes, the page is made again from all of it in the order of the addresses, so any order of loading gives the same page. Every kind, box and move gets a place under its address, like email.wire.inbox. What needs something that is not loaded says what it waits for and does nothing. A move is done by touching what the page made for it, or through Shape: {"do": "email.touch.send", "with": {"subject": "hi", "body": "there"}} or {"do": "email.touch.read", "pick": 1}. A move can also be handed in whole and goes once: {"from": "email.wire.sent"} answers what the box holds, and {"to": "email.wire.inbox", "with": {"subject": "hi", "body": "there"}} puts a thing in. That is the door for a reader outside the page; raw storage is not a door. Page shows what the loaded sheets make; Board comes back. A reload forgets what was loaded; what the boxes hold stays. A floppy carries the loaded sheets and what their boxes hold. The same sheets and the same floppy work in the generator for a terminal, /generator.py.

addresses./: The cover: a title and one line, whose word explore leads to /explore. The board is behind it.
addresses./explore: The whole field of interaction on one page: every door, address, script call, store and verb, and the grammar, written out from this file. A reader that runs no script gets one line there instead, which leads to this file.
addresses./serialize: Downloads what the board is and holds, as floppies.
addresses./deserialize: Asks whether to download a copy first, then takes floppies, wipes everything and rebuilds.
addresses./email/wire.json: A shipped JSON: the id email.wire is the file email/wire.json. The dot is the folder.
addresses./map: The card as a surface: paper, the whole page, no script. One select shows the card, or the live components standing on its elements in one of five themes that move nothing. Written by python3 generator.py map from map/card.json (where each element is on the art), map/live.json (the components and their connections, a snapshot) and map/on.json (which component stands at which element) and map/themes.json (colours, line and type only), loaded in any order.
addresses./generator.py: The generator for a terminal: python3 generator.py. The same sheets, moves and floppies as here, picked by number; it has no board.

ships.email.wire: What exists in an email: the kind mail (subject, body) and two boxes of mails, email.wire.inbox and email.wire.sent. Alone: what exists is shown and nothing can be done.
ships.email.touch: What whoever is at the device can do: send, read, look. With email.wire: fields and a button to send, and the rows of both boxes open.
ships.email.stub: A stub on the other end: ten seconds after a mail arrives in sent it puts an answer in the inbox. Unloaded, nothing answers, and a reader answers through Shape: {"to": "email.wire.inbox", "with": {"subject": the subject, "body": the answer}}.

sheet.id: Two levels, like email.wire. Every kind, box and move in the sheet has the address id.name, three levels. No two sheets share an id. The dot is the folder: email.wire is the file email/wire.json.
sheet.says: Words for a reader. The generator does nothing with them.
sheet.kinds: Each a name and the list of its parts. The first part is what a thing is called by.
sheet.boxes: Each a name and the kind it holds: a name in the same sheet, or an address.
sheet.moves: Each a name and one thing going from somewhere to somewhere, said with the five words below.
sheet.from: The box the thing is picked from. Left out, the thing comes from whoever is at the device, who makes it.
sheet.to: The box the thing is put in. Left out, the thing goes to whoever is at the device, who is shown it. A thing stays where it came from.
sheet.when: A box. The move then happens by itself for each thing that arrives there. The generator sees only what arrives through it.
sheet.after: A wait in seconds before the thing goes on.
sheet.with: Parts of the thing and the words they get, whatever they were.
sheet.nothing else: A sheet cannot name a screen, a key, a button, a layout or where a box is kept; each device's generator answers those its own way. A sheet that says anything else is refused.

script.board.serialize(size): Gives the floppies as a list of JSON texts; size is the most bytes on each, 1474560 if left out.
script.board.deserialize(floppies): Takes floppies back, as text or parsed, one or many, in any order; wipes everything and rebuilds when the set is whole. Does not ask first.
script.board.engine: The engine number written on every floppy.
script.the DOM: The board's buttons and fields are in the page from load and can be operated without showing it.
script.board.load(id or JSON): Loads a shipped JSON by its id, or a JSON handed whole.
script.board.loaded(): The ids of what is loaded.
script.board.page(): Shows the page the loaded JSONs make.
script.board.do(move): Does a move: {"do": address, "with" or "pick"}, or a move handed whole. Answers what was said.

grammar.from: start at one of: document, box, localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, cookieStore, caches, history, location
grammar.call: call a method on the current thing; "with" lists what is passed
grammar.get: read a property of the current thing
grammar.set: write a property of the current thing; "to" is the value
grammar.new: make a Response or a URL; "with" lists what is passed
grammar.as: give the current thing a name; "$name" passes it later
grammar.use: go back to a named thing
grammar.part: run a named list of steps from "parts"
grammar.entries: turn the current thing into name and value pairs
grammar.each: run steps on every member of the current list
grammar.gather: run several lists of steps and keep each result under its own name
grammar.words: {Name} and {Value} are filled from the run; {Name:uri} makes it safe in an address; {Value:before=} and {Value:after=} split at the first equals sign
grammar.keep: on a store: how it is kept on a floppy. "empty" is the shape that empties it; "each" is the shape that puts one thing back, with {name} and {value} filled from the record. A store that holds elements needs only "empty". A store with no "keep" is not kept.

stores.is: The page itself. Things made here are real elements, shown in the box. They are gone on reload.

verbs.does: Makes an element of the kind in Value (p, button, input, details, ul ...) and gives it the name.
Sets the thing's words to Value.
Takes away the attribute named in Value.
Puts the thing inside the thing named in Value.
verbs.none: one of them is not here

verbs.does: Shows the thing as the browser holds it.
Takes the thing out of the page.

stores.is: localStorage. Kept by this browser for this site until cleared; every tab of the site sees it.

verbs.does: Reads back what is kept under Name.

stores.is: sessionStorage. Kept for this tab only; survives a reload, gone when the tab closes.

verbs.does: Reads back what is kept under Name.

stores.is: IndexedDB. A database in this browser, here one table called things.

verbs.does: Reads back what is kept under Name.

stores.is: Cookies this page can see, through the browser's cookie store. Kept until the browser closes.

verbs.does: Sets a cookie called Name holding Value.
Deletes every cookie this page can see.

stores.is: The Cache store. Normally holds fetched pages; here each entry is made on the spot from Value, and nothing is fetched.

verbs.does: Stores a response holding Value at an address ending in Name.

stores.is: This tab's history. The address changes and nothing loads, as long as the steps stay among entries made since the page loaded.

verbs.does: Adds an entry: the address ends in #Name and the entry carries Value.
Rewrites the current entry in place.
Steps forward one entry, if there is one.

stores.not kept: The browser does not hand over a tab's history, so a floppy cannot rebuild it.

not wired.why: The browser asks the visitor first.
The browser must fetch a file to register one.
They need something on the other end.
